proposals.before: At Dunqiu a great downpour struck, and the emperor wanted to withdraw. Yanshou urged him, saying, "The Jin forces are camped on the river and dare not come out; if we press straight into Chunzhou and seize their bridge, Jin will not be hard to subdue."
proposals.after: At Dunqiu a great downpour struck, and the emperor wanted to withdraw. Yanshou urged him, saying, "The Jin forces are camped on the river and dare not come out; if we press straight into Chanzhou and seize their bridge, Jin will not be hard to subdue."
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou (also Danzhou), not Chunzhou; the mistranslation obscures the place-name.

proposals.before: By then the Jin army had already fallen back to Chunzhou; when Gao Xingzhou reached Xicheng, Yanshou led light troops out to give battle;
proposals.after: By then the Jin army had already fallen back to Chanzhou; when Gao Xingzhou reached Xicheng, Yanshou led light troops out to give battle;
proposals.reason: 澶州 is Chanzhou, not Chunzhou; same error as in the preceding unit.

proposals.before: At Dunqiu they encountered heavy rains; the emperor wished to withdraw the army. Yanshou remonstrated, saying, "The Jin army is encamped on the riverbank and dares not come out to fight; if we go straight into Chunzhou and seize its bridge, then Jin will not be hard to pacify."
proposals.after: At Dunqiu they encountered heavy rains; the emperor wished to withdraw the army. Yanshou remonstrated, saying, "The Jin army is encamped on the riverbank and dares not come out to fight; if we go straight into Chanzhou and seize its bridge, then Jin will not be hard to pacify."
proposals.reason: Literal field likewise mistranslates 澶州 as Chunzhou.

proposals.before: Just then the Jin army had already returned to Chunzhou; Gao Xingzhou reached Xicheng, and Yanshou led light troops to meet them in battle;
proposals.after: Just then the Jin army had already returned to Chanzhou; Gao Xingzhou reached Xicheng, and Yanshou led light troops to meet them in battle;
proposals.reason: Literal field likewise mistranslates 澶州 as Chunzhou.

proposals.before: Early in the Qingtai era he was made Duke of Lu, again became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and took charge at Xuzhou.
proposals.after: Early in the Qingtai era he was made Duke of Lu, again became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and took charge at Xu prefecture (Xuzhou).
proposals.reason: 許州 is Xu prefecture; bare 'Xuzhou' is easily confused with 徐州.

proposals.before: His father Kuai had been magistrate of Shuo.
proposals.after: His father Kuai had been magistrate of Tiao.
proposals.reason: 蓚縣 is Tiao (Tiáo), not Shuo; the place-name is mistranslated.

proposals.before: His father Kuai was magistrate of Shuo.
proposals.after: His father Kuai was magistrate of Tiao.
proposals.reason: Literal field also renders 蓚 as Shuo instead of Tiao.

decisions.reason: Focus unit has 若徑入澶州; 澶州 romanizes as Chanzhou (also Danzhou), whereas Chunzhou would be 春州. The proposed replacement corrects only that place-name and leaves the rest of the speech intact.
Focus unit has 適晉軍先歸澶州; the same 澶州→Chunzhou error as in s0049. Chanzhou matches the Chinese place-name and the rest of the sentence is otherwise faithful.
The literal likewise turns 澶州 into Chunzhou in Yanshou’s remonstrance; Chanzhou is the accurate English for 澶州 and leaves the surrounding wording unchanged.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 若徑入澶州，奪其橋，則晉不足平

decisions.reason: Literal 先歸澶州 must read Chanzhou, not Chunzhou; the proposed fix corrects only that mistranslation.

decisions.after: Early in the Qingtai era he was made Duke of Lu, again became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and took charge at Xu Prefecture.
decisions.reason: Focus unit has 鎮許州; 許州 is Xu Prefecture (around Xuchang), not 徐州. Bare “Xuzhou” invents the wrong place, but the proposed “Xu prefecture (Xuzhou)” is awkward and reintroduces the 徐州 reading; “Xu Prefecture” is the accurate, natural correction.
Focus unit has 令蓚; 蓚 (also 蓨) is Tiao county, whereas Shuo would be 朔. The proposed Tiao restores the place-name; the father’s name and office wording are otherwise unchanged.
The literal likewise renders 蓚 as Shuo; Tiao matches the Chinese place-name and leaves the rest of the sentence intact.
